analysis.title: Thursday, November 5th, was a day of extremes
key_insights: US long/short hedge fund net leverage fell 5% day over day on Nov 5, the 5th largest single-day decline since 2010, and is now in the bottom decile since 2010 (MS Prime Brokerage data).
Long/short fund active gross flow since June amounts to a -10.7% reduction relative to gross market value at end of June, the most in at least 10 years.

Hedge funds are now underweight AI stocks relative to market cap weights, though AI is still 32% of absolute exposures (MSXXAI Index constituents: AI tech beneficiaries, AI power names, key hyperscalers).
Levered ETFs had the largest amount to sell in data going back to 2007, bringing $57bn of US equity supply.
Retail selling of US equities in the first 90 minutes was the second largest since 2016, based on MS QDS estimates using public data.
Equities are trading in a more correlated fashion, which often signals that risk reduction is broadening out.
risk_factors: Broadening risk reduction across equities, as indicated by rising correlation.
AI stocks remain 32% of hedge fund absolute exposures despite the underweight versus market cap, so further AI deleveraging remains possible.

Hedge funds are underweight AI stocks versus market cap weights, with AI at 32% of absolute exposures.
